name: The Cultural Mandate and Vocation

objectives.text: Identify that God gave the first people the work of caring for the garden
Name the parts of God's command to Adam and Eve to fill the earth and rule over it
Give examples of everyday work at home and school that cares for the things God has made
Explain from Genesis that work was a good gift from God given before sin entered the world
Summarize the four parts of the Cultural Mandate as be fruitful, fill, subdue, and have dominion
Explain dominion as stewardship of creation that belongs to God rather than ownership that permits exploitation
Describe the pattern of six days of work and one day of rest that God set in creation and in the fourth commandment
Explain how Adam's naming of the animals shows people using God-given gifts to develop and order creation
Compare work before the Fall with work after the curse of thorns, sweat, and toil
Apply the command to do all work heartily as for the Lord and for his glory to ordinary classroom tasks
Explain what Scripture teaches about diligence, laziness, and working in order to provide for oneself and give to others
Analyze vocation as service to God and neighbor carried out in the callings of family, church, work, and community
Analyze the growth of herding, music, and metalwork in Genesis 4 as cultural development continuing in a fallen world
Explain how God renewed the command to be fruitful and fill the earth to Noah after the flood
Interpret Old Testament laws about land, trees, and animals as examples of how dominion includes care for creation
Compare the Cultural Mandate with the Great Commission in their scope, purpose, and relationship to each other
Explain the dignity of ordinary work using biblical examples such as Bezalel the craftsman and Jesus the carpenter
Explain how Reformers such as Luther and Calvin taught that every lawful calling, not only church office, is a place to serve God
Construct a theology of work that traces labor through creation, fall, redemption, and new creation
Evaluate views that treat secular work as less holy than sacred work in light of Scripture's teaching on vocation
Defend a biblical stewardship of creation against both exploitation of nature and worship of nature
Evaluate biblical principles for discerning a calling such as stewarding gifts, serving others, and seeking wise counsel
Evaluate contemporary attitudes that make work an idol or treat it as merely a means to money using the teaching of Ecclesiastes
Synthesize labor, rest, and dominion into an account of how the whole of human life can be offered as worship to the Creator

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (garden work, Genesis 1:28 summary, stewardship, pre and post Fall work, working as unto the Lord, vocation, creation care, Great Commission, dignity of work, theology of work, sacred and secular, nature-worship, synthesis). Merged the grade 2 recall into the kindergarten objective and replaced it with applying care of creation to daily work. Added work and rest pattern, Adam naming animals, diligence and giving, Genesis 4 cultural development, renewal to Noah, Bezalel and Jesus as workers, Reformation doctrine of vocation, discerning a calling, and work as idol. Added specific verse references and confessional anchors (WCF 4.2, WSC Q1, Q58, HC Q103, Q111, WLC Q141), keeping image of God content for the sibling sub-topic.
